decisions.reason: “Puffed up its fur” is the natural cat rendering of 털을 바짝 세우고; “bristled its fur” is awkward English.
BASE singularizes 파리; SOL’s “endless stream” overstates 끊임없이 and clashes with one-at-a-time entry.
decisions.replacement: The target of his anger was the flies that kept entering the house.

decisions.reason: 경계심 is wariness/being on guard; SOL’s “suspicious” narrows the emotion.
뻔한 is predictable/obvious, not inevitable.
Source is 미약한 마나; SOL adds unsupported “trace of.”
“Was it Sangdong Guild after all?” captures the interrogative 인가 more naturally.
당장 as “right away” fits Woojin’s colloquial anger; “immediately” is only a register shift.
신신당부 is stronger than “told”; “warned” matches the earnest admonition.
BASE calques 몸을 움직였다 and misreads 열심히 as “hurriedly”; SOL drops that beat and turns 기어가던 그때였다 into “Then—”.
decisions.replacement: Swallowing his curses, Hong Woojin wriggled with all his might. He was crawling deeper into a place no human eyes could reach when—

decisions.reason: Active “a strange sensation seized him” is cleaner prose for 사로잡혔다 without changing the float sensation.
“Shake off” is the English idiom; “shake his unease” is less natural.
Naturalizes 결정적인 계기/착각 without the Korean-shaped “decisive reason he convinced himself.”
“This fly’s looking” is more spoken and in-the-moment, matching 비실비실하네.
Keeps 대신 and 집 안을 가득 채웠다: snoring fills the house instead of laughter.
드르렁 is snoring; BASE “Grrrrr” reads as a growl.
놀랐던 is Woojin being startled while watching; SOL makes Taekyung the agent.
저런 is distal “that,” not “this.”
“Still harbored” is more natural English for the lingering 일말의 경계심.
Same snoring onomatopoeia as H015; “Grrrrr” is a growl.
총동원 is more than merely “using” the senses; “focusing” carries the effort.
“Now that the Link had been severed” states 링크가 끊긴 지금은 more clearly than the doubled dash.
돌아다녔다 is wandering/roaming, not merely walking around.
그중 … 없다 is absence among the insects just sensed, not a generic “anywhere.”
“Incessant buzzing” renders 쉬지 않고 without the clunky “continued without pause had stopped.”
얼씬도 못 하겠지 is not daring to show themselves; “stay away” flattens that image.
패밀리어라니 is an unmarked singular exclamation; pluralizing here is unsupported.
일종의 is “a kind of,” and “the caster’s skill” keeps 시전자/수준 explicit.
마법사도 마찬가지다 means mages are likewise not masters of everything; SOL invents “specialties.”
곳/한 군데뿐 is a place, not “people … from” the guild.
지시라면 is an open present hypothetical, not past-perfect “had been.”
Once 역린 is recast as a boundary, “crossed” is the natural English verb for 건드린.
다급해진다 is urgent/frantic, not merely that thoughts “raced.”
“By far too much” is unidiomatic; “had been underestimating … far too much” fits the comic realization.
Attaches Qi Sense to staying alert, fixing BASE’s misplaced modifier on the intrusion.
뻥 뚫린 is wide-open/uncongested, not empty.
SOL drops 한 번 (“once”).
Preserves 확연히 (“clearly”) and 화려했다 as splendid rather than lavish.
SOL omits 다른 가게들과, the contrast with ordinary shops.
성인이 아니라고 is “not adults”; SOL’s “you aren’t” can mean not allowed in.
Teen speech naturalizes 불량 as “broken” for a scanner giving a bad reading.
앳되어 보이는 is young-looking, not “underage.”
BASE’s “Customers to me are” is calqued; SOL turns 아니면 into “and” and drops 발급받은.
decisions.replacement: “My customers are Hunters or civilian adults who’ve been issued membership cards. Not high school punks like you.”

decisions.reason: 더더욱 intensifies presence at the Store; SOL adds unsupported “attracted.”
“Out front” is the natural US collocation for 앞에서 at an entrance.
확인 절차 is a verification procedure, not merely “verify it.”
Active “The Store stocked different items on each floor” is cleaner and still matches 층마다 … 다르다.
즐거운 시간 is “a pleasant time,” not specifically a visit.
“Thanks. Take care.” matches Taekyung’s casual 네, 고생하세요 to a worker.
Joining the 그러나 contrast into one sentence reads more smoothly without adding meaning.
Tighter English for 극소수다 and 이용할 수 있는 사람들 without changing the 0.1% split.
Observational “The employees … their products to customers” fits the scene; SOL is only a possessive shuffle.
일종의 is “a kind of,” not “essentially.”
SOL drops 성능 (“performance”) from the customer’s demand.
기본 수백만 원 대 is at least several million, not generic “millions apiece.”
Omitted subject is Store staff in general; “She” assumes Kim Seonhee served him last time.
극진한 접대 is devoted/attentive hospitality, not lavish luxury.
때가 왔다 is “the time had come,” a beat SOL flattens.
Drops the extra “who was” and uses “concerned about,” the natural collocation.
BASE’s “but” adds unstated contrast; SOL’s “A colleague” underspecifies the 입사 동기.
decisions.replacement: The colleague who had joined the company at the same time as her and worked at the Seoul branch was already a Team Leader. Whether it was luck or business savvy, every customer she encountered was apparently a big spender.

decisions.reason: BASE keeps 할인 but weakens 저렴한 as “reasonable”; SOL keeps “low” but drops the sale sense.
decisions.replacement: “It’s currently on sale as part of our summer promotion, so we’re offering it at the low price of 520,000 won.”

decisions.reason: “How much did a C-rank Hunter make a year again?” is more natural interior voice for 연봉이 어떻게 되더라.
BASE’s “cursing him” loosens 욕을 삼키며; SOL drops 집어 든 and the 그때였다 interruption.
decisions.replacement: The look on his face, as if parting with the money were killing him, was utterly obnoxious. Kim Seonhee swallowed a curse as she picked up the dagger when—
